service.py._Worker: Retain the local handles, live authority and requested outcome of one admitted run; this slot is not durable ownership proof.
service.py.RuntimeService._acquire: Exclusively lock the canonical business database for this serving owner and recover prior owner records; never let children inherit the lock.
service.py.RuntimeService.retry_start: Schedule only a newly recorded retry of the original queued request; an existing receipt returns its run without another scheduling decision.
service.py.RuntimeService.wait: Wait for this owner's existing worker without propagating observer cancellation into it; an absent local slot does not prove durable completion.
service.py.RuntimeService._end_tool_authority: Immediately disable the local slot and withdraw its live grant before potentially blocking persistence or native teardown.
service.py.RuntimeService._tool_authority: Ensure live tool authority ends on every exit from the worker scope, including errors and deadline cancellation.
service.py.RuntimeService._withdraw: Retire local tool authority, retain the requested outcome and request one native interruption; durable state is recorded separately.
service.py.RuntimeService._interrupt: Request native cancellation while recording an unavailable receipt by exception type; failure to receive a reply is not proof of closure.
service.py.RuntimeService.stop: Withdraw the observed local worker before recording cancellation and release its persistence gate afterward; no native completion is invented.
service.py.RuntimeService.reconcile: Share one shielded recovery task per exact intent and operation key, rejecting conflicting reuse and bounding outstanding local recovery work.
service.py.RuntimeService._execute.on_started: Retain the observed native-start flag and bind the reported thread and turn to the original attempt lease without granting new authority.

contracts.py.FrozenRunInput: Pair exact serialized attempt input with its content hash; the value alone does not certify provenance or permission.
contracts.py.text: Reject blank, non-string or oversized UTF-8 text without truncating the caller's value.
contracts.py.identity: Require a positive integer database identity, excluding booleans.
contracts.py.command_key: Validate a bounded stable operation identifier before it can name a replayable intent.
contracts.py.validate_correction: Validate the correction scope, expected version, original key, statement and attributed source kind before any persistence.
contracts.py.RunSpec: Describe one requested task execution and its context version; validated request data is not an attempt lease or execution permission.
contracts.py.RunSpec.__post_init__: Validate request identities and byte bounds without reading storage or admitting an execution.
contracts.py.WorkspaceBinding: Carry the selected repository and expected physical directory identity so admission and execution can revalidate the same workspace.
contracts.py.WorkspaceBinding.__post_init__: Validate supplied repository identity and absolute workspace syntax; physical directory verification belongs to the workspace boundary.
contracts.py.AttemptLease: Identify one owner's fenced attempt and expiry; mutation still requires store-side validation against current durable authority.
contracts.py.RunEvent: Expose one attributed durable runtime observation and its cursor; an event does not authorize work or prove the truth of model content.
contracts.py.EventPage: Return an ordered observation batch with its next cursor and continuation flag, without replaying the effects those events describe.
contracts.py.CommandSpec: Specify an argument vector, relative directory, deadline and per-stream capture bound; construction does not launch a process.
contracts.py.CommandSpec.__post_init__: Validate argument bytes, workspace-relative paths and explicit time/output ceilings before a command may be reserved.
contracts.py.CommandJob: Project one reserved command, captured binary output and separate local-closure evidence; exit code and closure may independently be unknown.
contracts.py.JobReservation: Return the original command receipt and whether this reservation newly permits dispatch; recovering a receipt never grants another launch.
contracts.py.native_outcome: Map a supported native terminal observation to review or reconciliation; native completion never means owner acceptance.
contracts.py.cancel_outcome: Choose the product state after cancellation intent, rejecting accepted work and preserving states that already require separate recovery.
contracts.py.invalidated_outcome: Invalidate queued or delivered work after context changes while sending active work to reconciliation rather than claiming it has stopped.

sqlite_runs.py._json: Serialize deterministic finite JSON for durable intent fingerprints and receipts; non-finite numbers are rejected rather than normalized.
sqlite_runs.py._digest: Hash the canonical serialized intent so an operation key cannot silently acquire different arguments.
sqlite_runs.py._duration: Require an explicit positive lease interval of at most120seconds, excluding booleans.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._transaction: Open only an existing database and commit or roll back one transaction; writes acquire the SQLite writer lock before yielding.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._existing_task: Validate and find a task within its project, raising RunNotFound instead of leaking another project's task.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._context: Read the stored task context revision, using the original version1 only when no context row exists.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._event: Append a versioned runtime task event in the caller's transaction and return its durable replay cursor.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._receipt: Recover the saved result for an exact project/task/key intent; conflicting reuse raises instead of creating another effect.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._save_receipt: Persist an intent hash and its result inside the same transaction as the effect it identifies.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.get: Read the current project-scoped run projection without granting authority or launching recovery.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.context_snapshot: Read one consistent task/context snapshot including attributed corrections, metadata changes and recorded answers.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._context_snapshot: Build the input context from current task metadata and ordered provenance records; metadata edits are not reattributed to the owner.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.task_runs: Return a bounded newest-first run history for one existing project task, without changing prior execution states.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.settle_inference: Record terminal usage for the original reserved attempt, preserving the greatest observation and unknown values while rejecting conflicting settled receipts.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._retire_closed: Retire a physically closed attempt and its grants, marking missing command/native receipts unknown rather than inventing terminal results.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._correction_intent: Build the canonical validated correction intent while keeping its replay key separate from the hashed request body.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.correction_receipt: Recover the original context version for an exact correction intent without applying the correction again.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._check_registration: Reject an admitted binding when its project repository registration is absent, inactive or points to a different recorded path.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.workspace_binding: Read the retained repository binding for a scoped run, returningNone only when that history has no binding.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._binding_view: Reconstruct the validated immutable workspace-binding value from its retained database fields.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.request_start: Record one retry intent only for the unchanged, unclaimed queued request; returnFalse for an already recorded retry instead of scheduling again.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.record_issue: Attach a bounded diagnostic only to the still-matching queued or failed/reconciling attempt; stale observations leave current work unchanged.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._attach_conversation: Bind an admission to a compatible active owner conversation and persist its original request/message link in the caller's transaction.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._deliver_proposal: Append the first linked proposal message as explicitly unaccepted; a repeated terminal observation cannot duplicate that delivery.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.claim: Atomically claim the existing queued request as a new fenced attempt; this operation alone does not dispatch a model.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.heartbeat: Extend only a currently authoritative attempt's lease and return its updated expiry without replacing its owner or fence.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.bind_grant: Bind an unexpired matching business grant to its original live attempt; a grant already bound elsewhere cannot be transferred.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.finish: Persist one exact native terminal observation after peer closure, revoke grants and deliver completed text for review without accepting the task.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._original_attempt: Validate an observation's original project, task, actor, owner and fence even when that attempt no longer has current mutation authority.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.attempt_active: Report whether current durable authority still matches the lease; absent or stale attempts returnFalse without mutation.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._job_view: Decode a command row into its bounded spec, binary receipts and independently observed local-closure flag.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._job_row: Read a project-scoped command with closure evidence from its own closed registered peer; a missing peer never proves closure.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.get_job: Inspect an existing project command and its retained output without revalidating execution permission or redispatching it.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.reserve_job: Reserve one command under the current attempt/workspace and bound peer, or recover the identical original receipt with dispatch disabled.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._owned_job: Require the command to belong to the lease's original attempt; receipt observation does not restore current execution authority.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.cancel_job: Record cancellation intent once for the original command, preserving unknown effects and never converting a request into physical closure.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.finish_job: Retain bounded append-only output from the original executor, reject conflicting terminal receipts and withdraw current authority when the exit remains unknown.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._withdraw: Advance the run fence and revoke its attempt grants in the current transaction; this state change does not terminate operating-system processes.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.expire: Retire an elapsed current run lease if necessary and return whether authority changed; no new attempt is started.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore._expire_current: Withdraw only an actually elapsed running lease, record the expiry event and preserve reconciliation until effects are known.
sqlite_runs.py.SQLiteRunStore.correct_context: Atomically apply an attributed, version-checked correction and save its original receipt; an exact retry returns the same version.

peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry.__init__: Use the existing run store as the transaction and authority boundary; constructing a registry creates no process or peer.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry._database_identity: Bind peer observations to the canonical database path and current device/inode, so a copied database cannot silently inherit control.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry._check_origin: Require the recorded database origin and, for open peers, the same boot and observer namespace before allowing physical control.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry.prepare: Register one allowed peer kind under a current lease before releasing any process; retain its origin and capacity checks atomically.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry._row: Find one registered peer by its opaque identity or raise RunNotFound; caller-specific authority checks remain separate.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry.inspect: Read retained peer metadata without spawning, closing or asserting current process liveness.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry._lease: Recover the original attempt identity and the peer's recorded fence for later authority validation; reconstruction alone is not authorization.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry.close: Prove closure of the originally bound namespace before recording closed state; validate origin and binding again around physical teardown.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry._closed: Persist a peer's closure reason and runtime event after the caller has established never-release or physical-closure proof.
peer_registry.py.PeerRegistry.command: Build the guard invocation for an existing registered peer; returning argv neither starts nor releases its payload.
peer_registry.py.AttemptPeers.__init__: Retain one attempt lease and its initially registered peer identities without claiming they have been spawned or closed.
peer_registry.py.AttemptPeers.claim: Claim a fenced attempt and register its initial peer scope in one transaction, before any native or business payload can run.
peer_registry.py.AttemptPeers.prepare: Register initial peers for an already authoritative lease, preserving host-only publication scopes without fictitious inference peers.
peer_registry.py.AttemptPeers.command: Construct the owned guard command for one of this attempt's initial peer kinds; execution remains the caller's responsibility.
peer_registry.py.AttemptPeers._rows: Read every retained peer for this attempt, including later command and Ken peers outside the initial identity map.
peer_registry.py.AttemptPeers.closed: Require every retained peer and initial identity to have recorded closure; a host-only scope may legitimately contain no peers.
peer_registry.py.AttemptPeers.aclose: Request closure of every retained attempt peer in worker threads and propagate failures; callers must not assume all peers closed after an error.
